item.content:encoded:
Are you a Master’s student passionate about sustainability, corporate social responsibility, social impact, philanthropy, and project management? L’Oréal is offering an exciting 12-month apprenticeship opportunity with La Roche-Posay, one of its leading dermatological beauty brands, beginning in January 2027.

The La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprentice – Junior Project Manager Sustainable Development & Social Impact opportunity offers students the chance to gain practical experience working on environmental sustainability, social-impact initiatives, philanthropic programmes, communications, and brand-cause projects within one of the world’s largest beauty companies.

The apprenticeship is based in Île-de-France, France, with the position associated with the La Roche-Posay/L’Oréal teams in the Paris region.

Successful candidates will receive €1,700 per month, partial public transportation reimbursement, one remote-working day per week, paid leave, access to L’Oréal’s learning platform, preferential employee purchasing benefits, and other workplace perks.

If you are interested in building a career in sustainability, corporate responsibility, project management, communications, social impact, or responsible business, this opportunity could provide valuable international corporate experience.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organisation: L’Oréal Groupe
  • Brand: La Roche-Posay
  • Division: L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty
  • Position: Junior Project Manager Sustainable Development & Social Impact / Sustainability Apprentice
  • Opportunity type: 12-month apprenticeship
  • Location: Île-de-France, France
  • Work arrangement: Full-time, with one remote-working day per week
  • Start date: January 2027
  • End date: December 2027
  • Monthly remuneration: €1,700
  • Public transportation: 75% of public transport costs covered
  • Paid leave: 1 day per month
  • Language: English mandatory; French highly desired
  • Application deadline: The posting is dated 31 August 2026. The vacancy page provided does not state a specific closing date, so applicants should apply as soon as possible while the position remains available.

About the L’Oréal La Roche-Posay Apprenticeship

L’Oréal is offering this apprenticeship to students who want to combine professional development with meaningful work in sustainability and social impact.

The role goes beyond traditional administrative or internship responsibilities. The selected apprentice will participate in projects covering three interconnected areas:

  1. La Roche-Posay Foundation and philanthropy
  2. Environmental sustainability and sustainable development
  3. Social impact and brand-cause initiatives

This means the successful candidate will gain exposure to environmental, social and philanthropic programmes while learning how a major international brand develops, implements, communicates and measures its impact.

The apprenticeship is particularly relevant for students interested in how large companies integrate sustainability and social responsibility into their business strategies.

Why La Roche-Posay?

La Roche-Posay is a leading dermo-cosmetic skincare brand within L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty.

The brand’s approach is based on the principle that health is the future of beauty, connecting scientific research, skincare innovation and social responsibility.

Through this apprenticeship, students will have an opportunity to contribute to initiatives designed to create positive environmental and social outcomes while gaining an understanding of how sustainability operates within an international corporate environment.

The role also provides exposure to external organisations, including NGOs and associations, as well as internal teams responsible for marketing, communications, research and innovation, and sustainable development.

Key Areas of Responsibility

1. La Roche-Posay Foundation and Philanthropy

One of the major components of the apprenticeship involves supporting the La Roche-Posay Foundation.

The apprentice will contribute to the development and implementation of philanthropic programmes supported by the Foundation.

Responsibilities include:

  • Contributing to the development of philanthropic programmes.
  • Supporting the deployment and implementation of Foundation initiatives.
  • Helping communicate philanthropic programmes internally.
  • Supporting external communications about Foundation activities.
  • Helping increase awareness of the Foundation’s programmes.
  • Supporting the team with day-to-day philanthropic activities.

This part of the role is particularly relevant to students interested in philanthropy, nonprofit partnerships, social impact, communications and programme management.

2. Environmental Sustainability and Sustainable Development

The apprentice will also contribute to La Roche-Posay’s environmental sustainability transformation.

This involves supporting initiatives designed to strengthen the brand’s sustainability commitments and communicating its environmental progress.

Potential responsibilities include:

  • Contributing to sustainable transformation projects.
  • Supporting sustainability initiatives.
  • Helping pilot key environmental initiatives.
  • Developing content related to sustainability.
  • Creating campaign assets.
  • Supporting internal communications about environmental initiatives.
  • Supporting external communications about sustainability achievements.
  • Helping communicate the brand’s environmental commitments to wider audiences.

This aspect of the position makes the opportunity particularly attractive for students interested in ESG, sustainability, climate action, corporate responsibility and responsible business.

3. Social Impact and Brand Cause

The third major area involves social initiatives, particularly programmes connected with oncology and support for cancer patients.

The apprentice will contribute to the development and implementation of social programmes and help communicate their impact.

Responsibilities include:

  • Supporting the development of programmes dedicated to oncology.
  • Contributing to initiatives supporting cancer patients.
  • Helping pilot social-impact initiatives.
  • Creating communication and campaign content.
  • Developing campaign assets.
  • Supporting internal communication.
  • Supporting external communication.
  • Helping communicate the achievements and impact of social programmes.

This gives the successful candidate an opportunity to understand how a global consumer brand can use its platform and resources to address societal issues.

Daily Responsibilities

In addition to the three principal areas of responsibility, the apprentice will provide day-to-day support to the Sustainability, Brand Cause and Philanthropic Foundation team.

This means the position can involve a variety of activities rather than being restricted to one narrow area.

The successful candidate should therefore be comfortable managing multiple priorities, collaborating with different stakeholders and adapting to changing project requirements.

What You Will Learn

The apprenticeship is designed to provide both professional and personal development.

According to the vacancy, the experience will provide a global and strategic understanding of the brand’s commitments to sustainability and social impact.

During the 12 months, the apprentice can gain exposure to:

  • Corporate social responsibility.
  • Sustainable development.
  • Environmental sustainability.
  • Social impact.
  • Philanthropy.
  • Project management.
  • Campaign development.
  • Corporate communications.
  • Stakeholder engagement.
  • Brand-cause initiatives.
  • NGO and association partnerships.
  • Environmental and social challenges.
  • International business operations.
  • Cross-functional collaboration.

The apprentice will also work with multiple departments and external stakeholders, creating opportunities to understand how sustainability projects are developed and implemented within a multinational organisation.

Collaboration and Stakeholder Exposure

One of the strongest features of this apprenticeship is its cross-functional nature.

The successful candidate will work with La Roche-Posay teams and L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty while interacting with external stakeholders such as NGOs and associations.

The role also provides interaction with internal departments including:

  • Marketing.
  • Communications.
  • Research and Innovation.
  • Sustainable Development.
  • Impact and Sustainability.

This type of exposure can be valuable for someone seeking a future career in project management, sustainability consulting, corporate responsibility, ESG, communications or social-impact strategy.

Who Is L’Oréal Looking For?

L’Oréal is looking for a Master’s student who is genuinely interested in sustainability, CSR, social responsibility and philanthropy.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate more than academic qualifications. The company is also interested in curiosity, communication ability, initiative, creativity and the capacity to work independently.

Key qualities and skills include:

  • Clear interest in corporate social responsibility.
  • Interest in sustainable development.
  • Interest in social responsibility.
  • Interest in philanthropy.
  • Curiosity about brand environments.
  • Curiosity about societal issues.
  • Results-oriented mindset.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Excellent written communication skills.
  • Excellent oral communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Data-analysis skills.
  • Proactivity.
  • Ability to work autonomously.
  • Creativity.
  • Entrepreneurial spirit.
  • Open-mindedness.

Language Requirements

English proficiency is mandatory for this position.

Strong English communication skills are therefore essential.

French proficiency is highly desired, making knowledge of French an important advantage for candidates working in France and interacting with French-speaking colleagues or stakeholders.

Candidates who do not speak French may therefore still be considered based on the vacancy’s stated requirements, but French language skills could strengthen an application.

Academic Requirements

Applicants must be:

  • Master’s students.
  • Studying at an engineering school, business school or university.
  • Available for a 12-month apprenticeship.
  • Available from January 2027 through December 2027.
  • Comfortable working in an English-speaking environment.

The opportunity is therefore specifically structured for students who are undertaking or entering a Master’s-level programme that supports an apprenticeship arrangement.

What Does L’Oréal Offer?

The apprenticeship provides a combination of financial compensation, professional development and employee benefits.

Monthly remuneration

The selected apprentice will receive:

€1,700 per month

This provides financial support throughout the 12-month apprenticeship.

Transportation support

L’Oréal will cover 75% of public transportation costs, helping reduce commuting expenses for the successful candidate.

Remote working

The position provides:

One day of remote working per week

This gives the apprentice some flexibility while maintaining regular interaction with the team.

Paid leave

The listed benefits include:

One day of paid leave per month

Learning and development

Apprentices will have unlimited access to L’Oréal’s My Learning platform.

This can support continuous professional development and allow participants to build additional skills during their placement.

Employee purchasing benefits

The opportunity also provides access to preferential prices through L’Oréal’s internal online store.

Other benefits include Friends & Family sales.

Depending on the campus, additional facilities may include amenities such as gyms and concierge services.

A Potential Pathway to a Permanent Career

Another particularly interesting feature of the opportunity is L’Oréal’s emphasis on developing early-career talent.

The company states that approximately 70% of its entry-level positions are filled by former interns and apprentices.

This does not guarantee a permanent position after the apprenticeship, but it demonstrates that apprenticeships can serve as an important entry point into the L’Oréal Group.

For students who perform strongly and demonstrate the skills, attitude and potential required by the organisation, the apprenticeship could therefore provide valuable exposure to future career opportunities.

L’Oréal’s Internship and Apprenticeship Environment

L’Oréal reports strong satisfaction among its interns.

According to the company’s internal satisfaction survey from June 2026:

  • 88% of interns said they were proud to work at L’Oréal.
  • 87% recommended L’Oréal for an internship.

These figures reflect the company’s stated internal survey results and highlight its emphasis on providing a positive early-career experience.

Recruitment Process

Applicants should be prepared for a two-stage recruitment process.

Stage 1: Recruiter Interview

The first stage is a 30-minute recruiter interview.

This stage is designed to introduce yourself and discuss the position and the L’Oréal Group.

Applicants should be prepared to explain:

  • Their academic background.
  • Why they are interested in L’Oréal.
  • Why they are interested in La Roche-Posay.
  • Why sustainability and social impact matter to them.
  • Their relevant skills.
  • Their career objectives.
  • Their availability for the January 2027 start date.

Stage 2: Interview With the Potential Manager

The second stage is a 45-minute meeting with the potential future manager.

This discussion is expected to focus more deeply on the missions of the position.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to demonstrate how their previous academic, professional, volunteer or project experience relates to sustainability, project management, communications, data analysis and social-impact initiatives.

Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable

This apprenticeship can be particularly valuable because it combines several career areas within one position.

A successful apprentice can gain experience in:

  1. Project management — supporting and piloting sustainability and social-impact initiatives.
  2. Sustainability — participating in environmental transformation projects.
  3. CSR — understanding how corporate responsibility programmes operate.
  4. Social impact — contributing to programmes supporting communities and cancer patients.
  5. Philanthropy — supporting Foundation programmes.
  6. Communications — developing content and campaign materials.
  7. Stakeholder management — interacting with internal and external partners.
  8. Data analysis — applying analytical skills to sustainability and social-impact work.
  9. International business — gaining experience within a multinational corporation.
  10. Cross-functional teamwork — collaborating with marketing, communications, research and sustainability teams.

For a student planning a long-term career in sustainability, consulting, project management, CSR, ESG or corporate strategy, this combination can be particularly useful.

Important Information for International Applicants

The position is located in France, specifically in the Île-de-France region.

Applicants should carefully consider the practical requirements of undertaking a French apprenticeship, including whether their Master’s programme and immigration/work status allow them to participate in the apprenticeship arrangement.

The vacancy itself specifies that applicants must be Master’s students and available for a 12-month apprenticeship from January to December 2027.

International candidates should therefore verify their eligibility for the relevant French apprenticeship and student/work authorization requirements before making arrangements.

AI at L’Oréal

L’Oréal also highlights its approach to artificial intelligence through its AI Charter.

The company describes AI as a tool that can support innovation while emphasising that technology should serve people.

L’Oréal states that it assesses the social, environmental and societal impacts of its AI systems and seeks to mitigate potential or actual harm.

This reflects the company’s broader position that economic and environmental performance should be considered together.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should apply through the official L’Oréal careers platform.

The application page is available through the job listing:

Apply for the La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprenticeship

Applicants should carefully review their CV and application before submitting.

L’Oréal notes that candidates can apply to up to three jobs within a rolling 30-day period.

The company also states that an application cannot be withdrawn once submitted, so applicants should make sure they select positions that genuinely match their career interests.

Applicants are also advised not to create another account using a different email address, as doing so could result in the account being merged and the application record being deleted.

Application Tips

To improve your application, consider the following:

1. Tailor your CV to sustainability

Do not submit a generic CV if you can avoid it.

Highlight experience related to:

  • Sustainability.
  • CSR.
  • Project management.
  • Research.
  • Data analysis.
  • Communications.
  • Social-impact initiatives.
  • NGOs or community projects.
  • Events and campaigns.
  • Stakeholder coordination.

2. Demonstrate measurable achievements

Where possible, show what you accomplished rather than simply listing your responsibilities.

For example, instead of only saying that you “supported projects,” explain what you coordinated, improved, delivered or achieved.

3. Highlight project-management skills

Because the position includes piloting initiatives, candidates should demonstrate their ability to plan, coordinate and deliver projects.

Examples could include academic projects, professional assignments, volunteer programmes, campaigns or community initiatives.

4. Show genuine interest in sustainability

Research La Roche-Posay and L’Oréal before applying.

Be prepared to explain why sustainability, social impact and responsible business are important to you.

5. Prepare for the recruiter interview

The 30-minute recruiter interview is an opportunity to demonstrate motivation and fit.

Prepare a clear introduction explaining:

  • Who you are.
  • What you study.
  • Your relevant experience.
  • Why you want this apprenticeship.
  • Why L’Oréal interests you.
  • Why La Roche-Posay interests you.
  • What you hope to learn.

6. Prepare examples for the manager interview

For the 45-minute manager interview, prepare specific examples demonstrating:

  • Leadership.
  • Initiative.
  • Problem-solving.
  • Communication.
  • Teamwork.
  • Data analysis.
  • Project coordination.
  • Attention to detail.
  • Working independently.

Important Dates

The apprenticeship is scheduled to run for 12 months:

January 2027 – December 2027

The job posting is dated:

31 August 2026

Application deadline

No specific closing deadline is stated on the vacancy page provided.

Because recruitment may close once a suitable candidate is selected, interested students should avoid waiting until the last minute and should apply while the vacancy remains open.

About L’Oréal Groupe

L’Oréal is one of the world’s largest beauty companies, with operations in more than 150 countries.

The company has a portfolio of international brands across four major divisions:

  • Consumer Products.
  • Professional Products.
  • Dermatological Beauty.
  • Luxury.

La Roche-Posay operates within the Dermatological Beauty division.

The Group describes its mission as creating beauty that moves, inspires and unites, while combining technology, science and natural inspiration to provide inclusive, responsible and forward-looking beauty.

L’Oréal also states that equal opportunity and diversity are important values within the Group and that it considers applications regardless of characteristics such as gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, social or cultural origins, health status, age or religion.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the L’Oréal La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprenticeship?

It is a 12-month apprenticeship focused on sustainable development, environmental sustainability, social impact, philanthropy and brand-cause initiatives at La Roche-Posay, a L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty brand.

When does the apprenticeship start?

The apprenticeship starts in January 2027.

When does it end?

The programme is scheduled to run until December 2027.

How much does the apprenticeship pay?

The advertised remuneration is €1,700 per month.

Where is the apprenticeship located?

The opportunity is in Île-de-France, France, with the vacancy description referencing the Levallois-Perret area.

Is English required?

Yes. English proficiency is mandatory.

Is French required?

French is highly desired, although the listing specifically identifies English as mandatory.

Who can apply?

The position is aimed at Master’s students studying at an engineering school, business school or university who are available for a 12-month apprenticeship beginning in January 2027.

Is this a remote position?

No. The position is not fully remote. L’Oréal offers one remote-working day per week.

Does L’Oréal cover transportation?

Yes. The advertised benefit is coverage of 75% of public transportation costs.

Is there a fixed application deadline?

No specific closing date is provided in the vacancy information supplied. The listing is dated 31 August 2026, so candidates should apply as early as possible.

Can applicants apply for multiple L’Oréal positions?

Yes. L’Oréal states that applicants can apply to up to three jobs within a rolling 30-day period.

Can an application be withdrawn?

According to the vacancy notice, applicants cannot withdraw an application once they have applied.

Final Thoughts

The L’Oréal La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprenticeship 2027 is a strong opportunity for Master’s students who want practical experience at the intersection of sustainability, social impact, philanthropy, communications and project management.

Rather than focusing on a single responsibility, the apprenticeship exposes the successful candidate to environmental sustainability, social programmes and philanthropic initiatives while providing opportunities to collaborate with marketing, communications, research, innovation and sustainable-development professionals.

The €1,700 monthly remuneration, transportation support, weekly remote-working option, paid leave, learning platform and other benefits make the opportunity particularly attractive for eligible students seeking international professional experience.

Perhaps most importantly, the position can provide a valuable foundation for a career in sustainability, ESG, CSR, project management, social impact, responsible business, corporate communications or consulting.

Students who meet the Master’s-level academic requirement, can commit to the January–December 2027 apprenticeship period and have a genuine interest in sustainability and social impact should consider applying early.

Apply through the official L’Oréal careers platform while the vacancy remains open.
